# Data Structures and Algorithms

A Java 21 library in which **every complexity claim is a test rather than a comment**. Built
from the fifteen-lecture syllabus of the sixth-semester DSAA course, clean-room, with no
historical source carried across. **224 JUnit 5 tests**, offline Maven build, no runtime
dependencies.

## The one decision everything follows from

Count operations; never measure wall-clock time. See
[[counted-complexity-assertions]] for the general idea and
[[clean-room-rebuild-from-specification]] for why the code is new.

Every structure takes a `Counter` and charges itself for each `comparison()`, `move()` and
`probe()`. A test then runs the algorithm over a doubling series of sizes, fits the measured
counts against seven candidate growth functions after dividing out the best constant, and
fails if the fit disagrees with the javadoc. Counts are deterministic for a fixed input, so
the same assertion passes identically on a fast machine, a loaded CI runner, and a laptop on
battery — which a timing assertion cannot.

## Eleven packages

| Package | Claim under test |
|---|---|
| `dsa.complexity` | the instrument itself, calibrated against sequences of known growth |
| `dsa.collections` | array vs linked indexing; appends amortise; the ring buffer's `n` dequeues stay linear |
| `dsa.sorting` | seven comparison sorts: which are stable, which have a bad input, which have none |
| `dsa.sorting.integer` | the `n log n` bound is about *comparison* sorts — counting sort makes zero |
| `dsa.search` | when sorting first pays for itself; quickselect is linear where sorting is not |
| `dsa.hashing` | amortised constant, and the conditions it is conditional on |
| `dsa.trees` | what balancing costs and what it prevents |
| `dsa.sets` | union-find with union by rank and path compression |
| `dsa.graphs` | which algorithm the weights and the acyclicity permit |
| `dsa.strings` | four ideas about what to keep after a mismatch |
| `dsa.techniques`, `dsa.npc` | greedy's counterexamples, and what "still exponential" is in numbers |

## The measurement that names the repository

Quicksort, twice, on the same already sorted array:

| n | `Pivot.LAST` | `Pivot.MEDIAN_OF_THREE` |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 8,121 | 882 |
| 512 | 130,809 | 4,548 |
| 2048 | 2,096,121 | 22,278 |

×4.0 per doubling against ×2.2 — quadratic against linearithmic, from one line of difference,
asserted rather than described. The same pair drives `docs/visual-guide.svg`.

## Two documented claims that the measurement contradicted

Both were corrected in the class comments rather than by loosening the assertion, which is the
rule recorded in `AGENTS.md`.

**Repeated heap insertion is not linearithmic on typical input.** The textbook `O(n log n)`
is a worst-case statement, routinely repeated as though it described the typical case. On
shuffled keys the fit comes out **linear**, because a random key lands near the bottom of the
heap and sifts up barely one level. The gap appears only on descending keys, where every
insertion is a new minimum; the suite now asserts both directions.

**Linear probing does not merely slow down — with the wrong keys it stops being constant per
operation.** With keys `"key0".."key8191"`, whose hashes are nearly consecutive, its measured
total is neither linear nor monotonic in `n`, while double hashing on the same keys is a clean
straight line. Linear probing was removed from the shared amortised-constant test and given a
dedicated one, rather than the shared assertion being relaxed for every implementation.

A third result is about the instrument rather than the algorithms: `n/4 + 1000` classifies as
**constant** at `n ≤ 512` and **linear** at `n ≥ 8192`. The fitter is right both times —
asymptotic behaviour is a claim about large `n`, and a measurement at small `n` is entitled to
disagree. The disagreement is a test, not a workaround.

## Failure modes are tests, not warnings

An adversarial hash whose every key collides; a delete that would orphan the rest of a probe
run without tombstones; sorted insertion degenerating a search tree to a linked list with
extra pointers; greedy change-making on `{1, 3, 4}` where the optimum is `3 + 3` and greedy
takes `4 + 1 + 1`. A structure whose guarantee is conditional is measured on the input that
breaks the condition — the same habit as
[[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]], enforced by the suite rather than by prose.

Making the cost of an operation part of its signature is
[[make-the-formal-object-observable]] applied to complexity: the `Counter` parameter is
intrusive on purpose, because a cost nobody can see is a cost nobody checks.

## Verification

A 2026-08-12 local audit passed Maven compilation and all 224 JUnit tests under JDK 21. Maven needed
the process-local `user.home` set to the owner profile because the sandbox reports `C:\` as Java's
home; that is environment configuration, not a code change. The existing SVG and its precise README
caption were preserved because they carry exact suite measurements rather than decorative estimates.

## Status and provenance

Local repository on `main`, one commit, **not pushed**. The syllabus supplied the topic list
and nothing else; see `NOTICE` and [[provenance-notice-file]]. Deliberate next steps in
`TASKS.md` — a red-black tree beside the AVL tree, a B-tree counting node accesses rather
than comparisons, an indexed priority queue to measure the constant-factor trade that lazy
deletion currently takes on trust in Dijkstra and Prim, and a space counter for the memory
claims that are still only prose.
